residents.name: Mira
lines: Morning, Amaal. Bramble’s decided the clean hay is a hat again.
Raeez helped mend the gate before he left. Said he would be back to help with supper.
Take what you need for the road. I’ll keep an eye on the animals.

residents.name: Idris
lines: The little goat arrived in a thunderstorm. Now she follows anyone carrying a bucket.
We give them a name before we give them a pen. Makes it feel like home.

residents.name: Sera
lines: Leave the tiny white flowers. The bees always find them first.
Your rose cuttings are doing beautifully. That stubborn one finally has a new leaf.

residents.name: Nani
lines: A garden is never finished, love. That is the lovely thing about it.
Raeez asked about flowers that would not open. I sent him to Lavendyr’s herbalist.

residents.name: Finn
lines: I counted the chickens twice. There were more the second time.
Stormy blinked at me. I think that means I am allowed to be his friend.

residents.name: Beatrix
lines: The hives are humming today. The roses will be pleased.
I left a jar by your door. For the journey, if the journey lasts longer than dinner.

residents.name: Oren
lines: The orchard baskets go to Sunveil on market day. Nothing beats a pear still warm from the sun.

residents.name: Tavi
lines: Fresh rolls, still warm! One for Amaal, and one for the friend who pretends he is not hungry.

lavendyr.name: Lavendyr Glade

residents.name: Maera
lines: These beds feed half the village’s remedies. The purple row is ready to harvest.
Looking for Raeez? I remember him asking after the flowers.

residents.name: Lina
lines: I label every cutting. I only forgot once.
Maera says a patient gardener makes a patient healer.

residents.name: Tamsin
lines: Fresh infusions this morning. The empty jars go back on the left shelf.

residents.name: Fenn
lines: I trade seeds for stories. Seeds keep better, usually.

residents.name: Rowan
lines: The tea leaves dry slowly in this shade. No rushing a good cup.

residents.name: Nessa
lines: The hens escape through that gate if anyone forgets it.

residents.name: Ollie
lines: I named the white hen Thimble. She never listens.

residents.name: Mirabel
lines: These cloth bags are for the next herb delivery.

residents.name: Galen
lines: Leaves in, bundles out. The whole lane smells lovely by sunset.

residents.name: Ada
lines: We used to know everyone by their garden. We still mostly do.

residents.name: Eira
lines: I came for a remedy and stayed for a chat. It happens every time.

residents.name: Bram
lines: A little water at the roots. The flowers can do the rest.

residents.name: Mira
lines: Your barn is stocked, Amaal. I can come by when you need an extra pair of hands.
Rosepetal is a quiet home. Let the animals keep you company.
A hen searches the farmyard for seeds.
The hen looks up, then resumes her work.
A farm cat keeps an eye on the path.

sunveil.name: Sunveil Grove

residents.name: Ilyas
lines: Morning deliveries from the grove, afternoon orders for the roads.
I keep a spare length of twine for every parcel. Something always works loose on a long road.

residents.name: Hanna
lines: The next batch is nearly ready. Follow the smell, not the queue.

residents.name: Orla
lines: A meal, a room, or directions? I can manage all three.

residents.name: Perrin
lines: This chair is for the inn. That wheel is for a wagon. No, I haven’t mixed them up.

residents.name: Tobin
lines: I’m allowed to sand the edges. The saw can wait.

residents.name: Soraya
lines: Something bright for a windowsill? These last well in shade.

residents.name: Dorian
lines: If it isn’t on the shelf, I can probably order it.

residents.name: Wren
lines: Clear a little space, please. These jars have had a long enough journey.

residents.name: Leah
lines: The first fallen apples are for the neighbours, not the compost.

residents.name: Joss
lines: I’m helping. Carrying the bread counts as helping.

residents.name: Mabel
lines: This square was quieter before the market. I prefer it like this.

residents.name: Theo
lines: I stop here for a night and leave with a week of supplies.

residents.name: Cora
lines: Have you seen the carpenter? He still has my gate hinge.

residents.name: Ari
lines: Keep a lane open by the fountain. People and deliveries both need it.

residents.name: Finn
lines: I counted the chickens twice. There were more the second time.
Stormy blinked at me. I think that means I am allowed to be his friend.

residents.name: Oren
lines: I bring the orchard baskets down to the square on market day. Nothing beats a pear still warm from the sun.
The market cat knows where the bakery is.
A small bird searches for crumbs.

signs.speaker: Tidepetal passenger quay
signs.text: Seabloom is across the gulf. Passengers use the central pier; working cargo stays at the eastern dock.

tidepetal.name: Tidepetal Quay

residents.name: Neris
lines: Passenger boat at the central pier. Cargo gets its own space.

residents.name: Dara
lines: A name on the manifest and a mark on the crate. That keeps the port honest.

residents.name: Bramble
lines: Seabloom is distant, but the passage is safe. Ready when you are.

residents.name: Orlo
lines: Mind the rope. This load is bound for the coast.

residents.name: Tessa
lines: The inland roads bring more flowers than fish to this quay.

residents.name: Meri
lines: Fresh from the river this morning.

residents.name: Flora
lines: A little colour for a long crossing?

residents.name: Copp
lines: A leaking barrel is everyone’s problem by the time it reaches the boat.

residents.name: Iven
lines: Rope, canvas, lamp oil. Ships are a hundred small errands.

residents.name: Sana
lines: Let the net dry before you fold it.

residents.name: Wes
lines: The Willow Quay has beds for late arrivals.

residents.name: Pella
lines: I packed early. Now I get to enjoy waiting.

residents.name: Rob
lines: Does the other port have the same seagulls?

residents.name: Arden
lines: These tea chests are travelling farther than I am.

residents.name: Faye
lines: The flower baskets soften even a warehouse wall.

residents.name: Dov
lines: I can tell who’s arriving by the voices on the pier.

residents.name: Tavi
lines: Fresh rolls for the crossing. And one saved for the friend who always says he is not hungry.
The quay cat follows the fish crates.
A river bird waits for an opportunity.
The bird has chosen the passenger pier.

seabloom.name: Seabloom Port

residents.name: Maren
lines: Welcome to Seabloom. Passenger arrivals stay clear of the cargo lane.

residents.name: Rook
lines: The coastal load goes left. The Tidepetal load goes right.

residents.name: Fern
lines: Give me room for one more crate and we’ll be finished.

residents.name: Borin
lines: The return passage leaves from this pier.

residents.name: Nerina
lines: The lighthouse saw the boats in before dawn.

residents.name: Iris
lines: There’s always one knot I haven’t found yet.

residents.name: Cato
lines: A good seam is quiet work that survives loud weather.

residents.name: Bea
lines: Come in when the salt wind gets into your bones.

residents.name: Sol
lines: Every boat gets the same light, whether we know the crew or not.

residents.name: Perry
lines: I help count the boats. I’m getting very good at it.

residents.name: Alda
lines: A map tells you where the road goes. Ask people what it feels like.

residents.name: Marina
lines: The wind bends these plants. It doesn’t stop them growing.

residents.name: Glen
lines: Tidepetal sends river goods. We send the coast back in return.

residents.name: Lio
lines: I’m heading inland after the crossing. A long road sounds rather good.

residents.name: Saff
lines: I have lived by this quay long enough to miss the noise when it stops.

residents.name: Tam
lines: I’m taking lunch to the netmender. Work still needs a pause.

residents.name: Beatrix
lines: The coastal hives are humming today. Even here, I plant a few roses to remind me of home.
The inland boats carry my honey back toward your valley. I like to think the flowers keep us connected.
The harbour cat is familiar with every stall.
A gull keeps the fish market under observation.
The gull prefers the lighthouse quay.
A gull patrols the quiet fishing pier.

residents.name: Iona
lines: Blue flowers on this bank, pink on that one. The river makes its own borders.

residents.name: Rafi
lines: Road supplies are inside. The riverside stalls are for slower shopping.

residents.name: Anwen
lines: The inn’s windows face the water. You’ll sleep to the stream.

residents.name: Silas
lines: A loose board sounds different. Listen when you cross.

residents.name: Mina
lines: These flower clippings will go to the young beds near the shop.

residents.name: Tariq
lines: The same crate crossed three bridges to get one street over.

residents.name: Della
lines: I keep a few travel journals by the door. They return with pressed flowers.

residents.name: Fin
lines: I’m checking the line, not staring at the water. There is a difference.

residents.name: Willa
lines: The blue thread is always the first to sell here.

residents.name: Nori
lines: A little jar goes a long way on the road.

residents.name: Elsie
lines: I live on the other bank. My favourite bench is on this one.

residents.name: Kit
lines: I count the deliveries. Boats are easy. Porters are harder.

residents.name: Rosa
lines: The bridges are where the town meets itself.

residents.name: Vale
lines: I meant to follow the road. These gardens are a fair excuse for a detour.

residents.name: Sera
lines: Leave the tiny white flowers. The bees always find them first.
Your rose cuttings are doing beautifully. That stubborn one finally has a new leaf.
A bird watches the stream.
The bird tilts its head toward the water.
The supply shop’s cat has no delivery schedule.

thornrose.name: Thornrose Hills

residents.name: Orin
lines: A cooking pot today, a wagon rim tomorrow. A forge serves more than swords.

residents.name: Pip
lines: The hot pieces go on that bench. I check twice.

residents.name: Mara
lines: The hill wind stays outside. The kettle does not.

residents.name: Holt
lines: Town is safe. Take care on the long road beyond the gate.

residents.name: Fara
lines: Rope, lamp oil, dry food. The hills use up all three.

residents.name: Gus
lines: Repair a wall before the stones learn to move.

residents.name: Bess
lines: Pebble could climb out. Fortunately she prefers the hay.

residents.name: Em
lines: That goat is pretending she’s never been fed.

residents.name: Tor
lines: We keep the heavy loads near the road, not up the stairs.

residents.name: Nell
lines: I brought the smith bread. He’ll remember to eat if someone does.

residents.name: Oswin
lines: A warm bench after a hill walk. That is luxury.

residents.name: Rin
lines: I’ll wait until my boots dry before I leave again.

residents.name: Idris
lines: The little goat arrived in a thunderstorm. Now she follows anyone carrying a bucket.
We give them a name before we give them a pen. Makes it feel like home.
A mountain goat waits for hay.
The goat watches the gate with interest.
The smith’s cat likes warm stone.

moonblossom.name: Moonblossom Hamlet

residents.name: Lumen
lines: One wick at a time. We make the evening together.

residents.name: Selene
lines: You can leave your boots by the door. There’s warm water inside.

residents.name: Yara
lines: The last pot is for anyone still on the road.

residents.name: Elowen
lines: A good story leaves room for the person listening.

residents.name: Eli
lines: I know this story. I want to hear it again.

residents.name: Moss
lines: The pale flowers show the path after the sky grows dark.

residents.name: Celyn
lines: The tall candles are for the inn. The little ones are for windows.

residents.name: Noa
lines: Some flowers save their best hours for the moon.

residents.name: Briar
lines: We leave a light on for our neighbours, too.

residents.name: Lark
lines: I came to return a book and stayed for tea.

residents.name: Aster
lines: This is the first place tonight that made me slow down.

residents.name: June
lines: The village stays peaceful. Leave the worrying for tomorrow’s road.

residents.name: Nani
lines: A garden is never finished, love. That is the lovely thing about it.
Before he left home, Raeez asked me about flowers that would not open. I suggested he speak with Lavendyr’s herbalist.
A cat settles into the evening.
A little bird gives one last call.

signs.speaker: Lavender Farmhouse
signs.text: Clean aprons hang beside a list of herb deliveries. The farmhouse table has space cleared for sorting the next lavender harvest.

signs.speaker: The Weaver’s Cottage
signs.text: Mirabel’s cloth-bag pattern lies beside a bundle of soft thread. The bags are sized for the herbalist’s dried-flower deliveries.

signs.speaker: The Gardener’s Cottage
signs.text: A watering rota is pinned beside muddy gloves. Tiny sketches show which beds need their seedlings thinned.

signs.speaker: The Drying House
signs.text: Bundles of herbs are listed by the day they were hung. A reminder says to keep the drying room airy and the damp bundles apart.

signs.speaker: The Wheelwright’s Home
signs.text: Wheel measurements cover a scrap of board. A small drawing shows exactly where yesterday’s cart began to wobble.

signs.speaker: Rosewood Cottage
signs.text: A mending basket sits beside a bowl from the market. The windowsill has been cleared for a pot of cuttings.

signs.speaker: The Orchard Family Home
signs.text: Oren’s orchard tally sorts apples from pears. A basket by the table is marked for the next trip down to the market square.

signs.speaker: The Flower Seller’s Cottage
signs.text: Soraya’s bouquet orders are tied with ribbons from the stalls. A pencilled note says to save the short stems for windowsill jars.

signs.speaker: The Market Storehouse
signs.text: The market tally separates stall deliveries from empty baskets. Someone has counted the seed sacks twice and signed both totals.

signs.speaker: Honeysuckle Cottage
signs.text: A cup has been left beside an unfinished letter. The writer pauses halfway through a description of the golden trees outside.

signs.speaker: The Baker’s Family Home
signs.text: The family recipe book is open at the everyday loaf. Floury fingerprints stop at a note about saving enough dough for breakfast.

signs.speaker: The Bridgekeeper’s Cottage
signs.text: River levels are marked beside the bridgekeeper’s breakfast cup. The newest note records a loose rail already added to the repair list.

signs.speaker: The Gardener’s House
signs.text: Pink and blue flower beds have separate watering notes. A neighbour has added a small thank-you for last week’s spare seedlings.

signs.speaker: The Weaver’s House
signs.text: The weaver’s measurements are weighted with river stones. Finished cloth is folded away from the open window and its drifting petals.

signs.speaker: The Fisher’s Cottage
signs.text: A river sketch marks the quiet pools and the busy crossings. Net repairs are listed beneath a reminder to leave the bridge clear.

signs.speaker: The Traders’ Storehouse
signs.text: Goods from both banks are counted on the same manifest. Crates for the ports are marked separately from the village deliveries.

signs.speaker: The Honey Seller’s Home
signs.text: Honey jars are tallied beside a sketch of the flowering riverbank. The seller has noted which hives need fresh frames.

signs.speaker: Pinegate Cottage
signs.text: Boots dry beside a carefully swept doorstep. A folded scarf waits with a note reminding its owner that the hill wind turns cold.

signs.speaker: The Stoneworker’s House
signs.text: A stone pattern is pencilled beside the day’s measurements. The smallest offcuts have been saved for repairing a neighbour’s garden edge.

signs.speaker: The Goatkeeper’s House
signs.text: A feed tally lists both mountain goats by their markings. Beside it, a firm reminder says to latch the paddock gate after every visit.

signs.speaker: The Hill Storehouse
signs.text: Hill deliveries are stacked by destination. Rope, grain and lamp oil each have a tally for the next journey over the pass.

signs.speaker: Willow Cottage
signs.text: A willow leaf has landed beside an open letter. A small cushion has been moved into the last warm patch of evening light.

signs.speaker: The Stream Gardener’s Home
signs.text: The stream gardener’s notes ask for soft banks and room for the water. Spare cuttings are wrapped in damp cloth for a neighbour.

signs.speaker: The Candle Maker’s Cottage
signs.text: Wick lengths and cooling times fill the candle maker’s page. A short row of finished candles is marked for the tea house.

signs.speaker: The Night Florist
signs.text: Pale flower orders are paired with dark ribbons. The florist has noted which blooms keep their scent after sunset.

signs.speaker: The Netmender’s House
signs.text: A net pattern marks the worn knots in red. The repaired sections are counted before the nets go back down to the river boats.

signs.speaker: The Cooper’s Workshop
signs.text: Barrel hoops and stave measurements cover the cooper’s bench notes. The next empty cask is marked for the riverside warehouse.

signs.speaker: The River Florist
signs.text: Willow sprigs sit beside the river florist’s ribbon list. Small bouquets are marked for the passenger quay rather than the cargo boats.

signs.speaker: The Ship Chandler
signs.text: Rope lengths, lamp oil and spare hooks fill the chandlery list. The ferry crew’s supplies have their own marked bundle.

signs.speaker: The Ferryman’s Family Home
signs.text: A sailing rota lies beside the family meal list. Somebody has circled the evening crossing and written “keep a bowl warm”.

objects.label: Tea table
objects.placementPurpose: Right-side dining recess; central entrance aisle kept clear

objects.label: A seat by the table
objects.placementPurpose: Right-side dining recess; central entrance aisle kept clear

signs.speaker: The Tea Merchant’s Home
signs.text: Tea samples are labelled by scent and steeping time. A small tin has been set aside for a neighbour who likes the gentlest blend.

signs.speaker: The Sailor’s Cottage
signs.text: A tide sketch is tucked inside a half-written letter. Clean socks hang where the next morning’s sun will reach them.

signs.speaker: The Cargo Clerk’s Home
signs.text: A spare cargo tally lies beneath the evening paper. The clerk has crossed out the work totals and begun a household shopping list.

signs.speaker: The Sailmaker’s Workshop
signs.text: Sail measurements are held flat with smooth stones. A chalk line marks the panel that needs mending before it returns to the boat.

signs.speaker: The Fisher Family Home
signs.text: Today’s catch is counted beside tomorrow’s tide. A family note asks whoever wakes first to put the kettle on before checking the nets.

signs.speaker: The Traders’ Exchange
signs.text: Exchange tallies compare incoming grain with outgoing coastal goods. Each trader has signed beside the crates they collected.

signs.speaker: The Map Seller’s House
signs.text: A coastal chart is open beside a stack of folded maps. Pencil marks distinguish the passenger piers from the cargo landings.

signs.speaker: The Coastal Gardener
signs.text: Marina’s planting notes favour low roots and shelter from salt wind. A pressed sprig shows how the leaves have bent toward the sun.

signs.speaker: Saltgrass Cottage
signs.text: A salt-stiff coat hangs beside a brush for sandy boots. The household list begins with fresh water and ends with a neighbour’s birthday.

signs.speaker: Seaglass Cottage
signs.text: A few smooth pieces of sea glass weigh down a letter. Someone has sorted them by colour while waiting for the kettle.

signs.speaker: The Keeper’s Family House
signs.text: Sol’s lighthouse round is pinned beside Perry’s boat count. A warm scarf has been left ready for the next windy evening.

signs.speaker: Seabloom Lighthouse
signs.text: The keeper records each safe arrival beside the lamp check. Tidepetal and Seabloom share a page full of careful tide marks.

objects.label: Fresh hay for the rescued animals

signs.speaker: Rosepetal Rescue Barn
signs.text: A fresh brush hangs beside a list of names. Every animal here was brought home by somebody who refused to leave it behind.

signs.speaker: The Rose Glasshouse
signs.text: Tiny wooden labels read: moon peas, winter roses, and one hopeful experiment marked “For Amaal”.

objects.label: A supper table set for neighbours

signs.speaker: Mira’s Farmhouse
signs.text: A loaf cools beside the window. Outside, someone is calling for the missing blue watering can.
